Review of SGP

 Student growth percentiles (SGPs) are most often calculated
 for grade level cohorts of students taking annual assessments
 in one or more content areas [Betebenner, 2009].
 For example, in Indiana SGPs are currently calculated in
 Mathematics and English/Language Arts in grades 4 to 8.
 Nothing prevents one from calculating an SGP using 10th
 grade as the dependent variable and 8th, 7th, . . . grades as
 independent.
 Need to consider differences in what is being calculated

SGP Analysis in 10th grade

 A 10th grade growth percentile represents a conditional
 probability across two years instead of one.
 Massachusetts has calculated these SGPs for 2 years and
 reports them to high schools.
 Because they quantile what has taken place across two years,
 attributions of responsibility (i.e., teacher or school
 accountability) are more tenuous.
 Possible to calculate a median SGP for only those students
 continuously enrolled for two years at the school to “tighten”
 the argument.
